# The overpaid invoice again, edited — the entry description differs, so the
# import unposts and rebuilds it — with the same payment block it came in on.
#
# This is the shape the marked-orphan tier exists for. Unposting leaves the
# transaction carrying two splits a retarget could place: the settlement just
# orphaned, and the 100.00 residue this same invoice parked as the customer's
# credit. Both are live and hold no document, so counted together they read as
# ambiguous and an ordinary edit of an overpaid invoice becomes unimportable —
# with the remedy reachable only by re-exporting. Only one of the two was ever
# this invoice's settlement, and only the mark says which.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.

invoice "INV-USD-RETARGET"
	customer_id: "C-US"
	currency: USD
	date_opened: 2026-01-05
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-05
		description: "Consulting, revised"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-01-05
		due: 2026-02-05
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
		memo: "Invoice INV-USD-RETARGET"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		date: 2026-02-25
		amount: 200
		bank_account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
		txn_guid: "TXN_GUID"
		prepayment: 100
		memo: "Payment for INV-USD-RETARGET"
